pool.text: Royal Navy Captain John Moresby became the first Briton to see Port Moresby.
Reverend William George Lawes joined Polynesian teachers and built a mission house.
Special Commissioner Peter Scratchley arrived to choose the site for the colonial capital.
Surveyor Walter Cuthbertson laid out a gridiron plan for townships Granville West and Granville East.
The first butcher's shop and grocery store opened in the growing settlement.
Port Moresby was successfully linked by radio communication to Thursday Island.
Electricity was introduced to the town for the local residents and administration.
A piped water supply was provided to improve the infrastructure of Port Moresby.
The Territory of Papua and New Guinea was formed under a single administration.
Port Moresby was granted city status with Oala Oala-Rarua becoming Lord Mayor.
Papua New Guinea became an independent country with Port Moresby as capital.
The census return registered a population of 120,000 residents in the city.
Prince Charles opened the new National Parliament Building blending traditional and modern technology.
An oil company set up by the United States began to export resources.
Port Moresby hosted the major international APEC summit bringing world leaders.
Al Jazeera described Port Moresby as one of the most dangerous cities.
The urban population grew to 756,754 people at the national census.
